intro.heading: The read
intro.body: Tomball arrives 3–0 with a 122–26 scoring margin and a ground game averaging 290 yards. Ian Thomas has 641 yards from scrimmage and nine touchdowns in three games; Klein Cain is 2–0 after an open week and averaging 43.5 points. Dave Campbell’s latest computer rankings place Tomball No. 45 and Cain No. 83, with the model favoring Tomball by three.

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: Through two wins, Hanks has 272 passing yards and three passing touchdowns plus 160 rushing yards and two scores. He also has 69 receiving yards and a touchdown, giving Cain a quarterback who can change roles without leaving the field.

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: Johnson leads Cain at 94.5 rushing yards per game through two wins. His 110-yard opener established the senior as the steady backfield complement to Hanks’ multi-position production.

players.name: Cooper Karns
players.copy: Karns has 147 receiving yards through two wins, including 110 yards and a touchdown at Humble. He gives Hanks an established target when Tomball commits extra bodies to the run.

players.name: Trevon Johnson
players.copy: Johnson has 316 rushing yards and five touchdowns through Tomball’s 3–0 start. The 6-foot, 205-pound senior gives the Cougars a second back averaging more than 100 yards per game beside Ian Thomas.

players.name: Ian Thomas
players.copy: Thomas is the centerpiece of this matchup: 505 rushing yards, 136 receiving yards and nine touchdowns in three games. He erupted for 240 yards from scrimmage and four scores against Klein Forest. The four-star junior is 247Sports’ No. 1 running back and No. 39 overall prospect in the 2028 class; his father, Rodney Thomas, starred at Texas A&M before a six-year NFL career.

players.name: Andres von der Meden
players.copy: Von der Meden committed to Texas A&M on June 8, and Rivals lists him as the No. 5 kicker in the 2027 class. Against Cinco Ranch he averaged 65 yards on six kickoffs and 44.5 yards on four punts; all five of his recorded kickoffs against Klein Forest went for touchbacks.

recapNotes: Quarterbacks coach Aiden Upchurch said before kickoff that Klein Cain would need to feed off homecoming energy and execute against a respected Tomball team: "Our key to victory tonight will be our level of execution. We feel like we have a good game plan, but we know Tomball is good too. If we can execute the way we know we can it'll be a great game." The Hurricanes did on homecoming night.
Quarterback Jace Hanks (#9) ran the offense all night. Tomball had no answer for him.
The game turned chippy. Personal fouls and unnecessary roughness penalties piled up, and Earl Oguinn Jr. (#1) was ejected in the fourth quarter after throwing a punch following a scuffle.
Memorial Stadium was packed for a big Klein Cain win.

final.headline: Klein Cain beats Tomball, 55–38
final.byline: Cain Game Day desk · Updated 10:35 PM CT
final.body: Klein Cain beat Tomball 55–38 at Klein Memorial Stadium on Sept. 18, a 17-point win. Klein Cain is 3–0. Dave Campbell’s Texas Football had Tomball by 3; Klein Cain won by 17.
